fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime conspicuity of the HAWK display against competing background elements is a genuine, scheme-relevant safety issue at a pedestrian-crossing arterial, with a credible mechanism (delayed/missed stop decision exposing crossing pedestrians).
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal driver-confusion claim is supported by a verbatim quote in EV-US-001 tied to the recorded Speedway Blvd/Rook Ave site-specific issue, satisfying the quote requirement for full credit.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern with no normative_basis_note, keeping it distinct from any MUTCD/FHWA compliance question per us-fhwa semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Retroreflective border installation is a specific, actionable, viable final-design-stage countermeasure targeted at the exact location and the nighttime-discrimination problem raised.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the relevant VRUs—are explicitly identified and their exposure via late driver detection is reasoned through, so vulnerable-user impacts are substantively considered.

justifications.substance: Real VRU exposure risk—elderly pedestrians still clearing when conflicting releases begin—at the corridor's highest-pedestrian-collision HAWK sites is substantive for a final-design audit.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim ('pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') is supported by a verbatim quote from EV-US-016, with recorded case-study input tying the issue to these exact six sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a categorical safety_concern with no compliance conflation; verifying walking-speed assumptions behind signal timing sits squarely within FHWA final-design RSA scope.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific (all six named HAWK sites), actionable (reprogramme clearance intervals), and viable pre-activation at final design; citing a target reduced walking speed value would strengthen it further.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are the explicit focus of the finding: pedestrians and elderly pedestrians are named road users, the category is vru-specific, and their clearance-phase exposure is directly addressed.
